title: Ambiguous household - 'the Smiths' matches two households; blocked pending human disambiguation
scenarioRefNote: Maps to scenarios.yaml `ambiguous-instruction` (a household or bank instruction is ambiguous; blocked pending human disambiguation OUTSIDE the model). This is the canonical multiple-Smiths ambiguity named by the v3 build sequence (prompt 13 re-baseline note).

signoff.note: Expected outcomes are product truth subject to captain signoff. Draft rules that the model NEVER guesses between candidate households - the ambiguity becomes a structured human question, never a probabilistic pick. Captain reapproved the explicit evidence-completeness matrix and canonical UTC timestamps on 2026-07-28.

trigger.description: Advisor enters: 'The Smiths need $75,000 for their home renovation by August 15.' The advisor's book contains TWO Smith households: Robert & Ana Smith, and the Smith Family Trust.
trigger.maskedRequestSummary: distribute 75000 USD for home-renovation; household slot has two candidates (tokenized)

householdEvidence.summary: Directory lookup for 'Smith' in the requesting advisor's book returns two candidate households: subject:smiths-robert-ana and subject:smith-family-trust. Neither is a uniquely better match.

householdInstructionsNote: No household-instruction versions can bind while the household slot itself is ambiguous - pinning either candidate's instructions would presuppose the answer to the human question. Recorded as silence, never filled in.

expectedAuthority.note: A blocked decision carries no authority and no execution plan (v3 invariant 8). Disambiguation is a human act recorded as evidence, not an approval stage.

expectedExecutionEligibility.reason: The household slot is ambiguous; no input bundle can be completed until a human selects the intended household.

blockers.explanation: 'The Smiths' matches two households in the requesting advisor's book; Verin does not guess between candidates.

expectedExplanationNodes.summary: Two candidate households match 'the Smiths': Robert & Ana Smith and the Smith Family Trust. Both candidates are shown with distinguishing context.
Verin asks the advisor a structured question (which household?) instead of guessing - the resolving affordance IS the question, and the answer is recorded evidence attributed to the advisor.

expectedLedgerEvents.note: The household-directory snapshot with both candidate refs is pinned - the ambiguity itself is recorded evidence.
Blocked decision carrying the ambiguity's structured human question as its resolving evidence; no authority, no execution plan.

expectedVerificationState.currentReason: No execution occurs until the advisor resolves the household identity
expectedVerificationState.note: No execution occurs. The advisor's recorded answer resolves the block and evaluation re-runs with the household bound - the disambiguation is attributed, timestamped evidence, not a silent retry.
